title: Stop Getting Blindsided By Bills You Knew Were Coming
hook_text: YOUR CAR BILL ISN'T A SURPRISE

beats.say: Your car registration isn't a surprise bill. It just arrives like one.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a lone car key resting on wet asphalt under harsh sodium streetlights.

beats.say: Every single year, predictable bills feel like financial emergencies. Why do we keep paying for them with panicked savings?
beats.visual: Low angle silhouette of a person standing alone in a dark kitchen, illuminated only by open refrigerator light.

beats.say: When a $3,000 bill hits a 24% APR credit card, paying minimums costs $4,887 in interest.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a credit card edge on a steel desk in cold fluorescent light.

beats.say: Most people assume they need a higher income. But you actually just need a simple sinking fund.
beats.visual: High angle shot of an empty highway at night with mist drifting across lane markers.

beats.say: Here's the 15-minute system to neutralize every yearly expense before it ever hits your mailbox.
beats.visual: Silhouette of hands holding a dark smartphone screen in a fog-filled room during blue hour.

beats.say: Step one. Choose one recurring bill due later this year, like car registration or holiday gifts.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a dark calendar on a wooden table lit by a single desk lamp.

beats.say: Take the total dollar amount and count the exact months remaining until that bill is due.
beats.visual: Cinematic shot of heavy rain slanting across a dark suburban street under towering utility poles.

beats.say: Step two. Divide that total cost by the remaining months to calculate your exact monthly requirement.
beats.visual: Low angle view of an empty concrete bridge under single practical light at midnight.

beats.say: Divide that figure by your paychecks per month so you know what to save each payday.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of water droplets running down a dark glass window pane.

beats.say: Step three. Open a separate sub-account and automate that exact transfer on every single payday.
beats.visual: Silhouette looking out from a high-rise tower edge over a foggy city skyline.

beats.say: When the invoice lands, the full balance is already sitting there, completely paid for without stress.
beats.visual: Cinematic wide shot of an empty asphalt road reaching into a dark horizon under pale blue twilight.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you, so no bill arrives like a surprise again.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of red car taillights fading into dark night fog on a wet road.

caption: Stop letting annual bills destroy your emergency fund. Here is the 3-step sinking fund formula to automate every recurring bill today.
description: Annual bills like car registration, insurance renewals, and holiday gifts feel like sudden emergencies when paid all at once. This 15-minute sinking fund system splits irregular expenses into payday automated transfers so you never pay debt interest on predictable life expenses.
first_comment: Which annual bill always seems to sneak up on your budget?

facts.claim: Paying only minimums on a $3,000 credit card balance at 24% APR costs $4,887 in interest.
facts.basis: $3,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum (1% + interest, min $25): 183 months (~15 years), $4,887 interest

loop_map.stakes: Predictable annual expenses turning into credit card debt emergencies.
loop_map.big_question: Why do predictable bills constantly trigger financial panic and high credit card interest?
loop_map.assume: You need a higher income to absorb large annual expenses.
loop_map.reveal: You just need a sinking fund to split the bill across remaining paychecks.
